Any other file stays untouched.

PURPOSE. The author's rule: at a decision point in a scene, if the state of the NEXT scene does not follow from where the chosen branch leaves off, something is broken. Build a story-agnostic report for an INCIDENT anchor that shows, for each branch, (1) what the branch does inside its scene and whether it leaves an authored way out, and (2) whether the next scene's starting state follows from where the branch left off. Existing tools to reuse (read them first): `exit_transitions`, `_anchor_item`, `_baseline`, `custody_checks`, `_reachable_facts` and the Flag/render style in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/gap_rules.py; `producers()`/`consumers()` in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/dependencies.py; the trace in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/situation_trace.py; the impact report in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/impact_report.py (reuse its `_source_location` style: cite a file and line ONLY for a line that defines the record; otherwise cite nothing, never invent a location). This is a Layer 3 tool: deterministic, may run the real engine, quotes evidence, is reported and never blocks a build. Words: write "result", never "flag".

BRANCHES. An incident (class Incident in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/models.py) has `outcomes` (each names a storylet, a realization, `advantages`, `costs`), a `recovery_storylet_id` and a `missed_window_event_id`. Treat each outcome, the recovery path and the missed-window path as one branch each. Find each branch's claims through the realization/storylet ids (the claim source is `KnowledgeDefinition.source`) and its effects through the claim's `establishes`; the missed-window branch is a pacing event with `effects`. The NEXT scene is the target of the transitions whose `source_scene_id` equals the incident's `scene_id` (use the incident's `successor_transition_id` when it is set). If there is no next scene, say so in the report and skip part (2).

CHANGE TO /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/dependencies.py. Add an optional `scene_id: str | None = None` field to the `Consumer` dataclass (last field, so every existing call and test keeps working) and fill it in `consumers()` wherever the reading record has a scene (pacing events, transitions via source scene, storylets, scene entry variants, claims via available_in_scenes when exactly one scene, and so on). Do not change any existing consumer text. The consumers of scene entry variants (`SceneMetadata.entry_variants[].requires`) must exist in `consumers()` with kind 'wording' if they do not already.

REPORT, for `render_branch_report(root: Path, incident_id: str) -> str`, per branch:
A. WHAT IT DOES. The branch id, the quoted delivery text of its realization claim (first sentence is enough), the facts it sets with each fact's `purpose` from the package's fact declarations, and its declared advantages and costs. For each declared cost or advantage say whether the realization actually sets it and whether anything reads it (use `consumers()`); an unread declared cost or advantage is a result worded in story terms, for example: "The branch declares cost X ('<purpose>') but nothing later reads it, so the cost has no effect." Do not use the word flag.
B. WAY OUT. Using the real transition triggers, report whether the next-scene transition(s) can fire after this branch (assert the branch's facts on a baseline state as `_baseline`/`_reachable_facts` do, then evaluate the triggers; follow how the engine evaluates them). If none can fire and nothing authored remains, that is a dead end: say so as a result with the unmet trigger facts.
C. HANDOFF CONTINUITY (the core). Build the world after the branch: bootstrap the runtime state for the incident's scene (as `_baseline` does), assert the branch's facts, apply `apply_world_effects`, record the world snapshot (parent/place of the protagonist, every character and group, every item, the protagonist's companions, and who holds each item). Then apply the next scene's entry with `apply_scene_placements(package, facts, next_scene_id)` from /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/runtime/world_model.py and take a second snapshot. List EVERY change between the snapshots: protagonist moved, character moved, item changed place or holder (an item the protagonist held that ends elsewhere is a loss of custody, state it that way), companion cleared or added. For each change say whether the transition has authored `bridge_text` for it (the transition's bridge text in the scene metadata of the source scene) and quote that text as evidence; a change is an unexplained move result only when it is not just the protagonist arriving at the next scene's location. Compare across branches: a move that happens in some branches and not others is reported with the branches named. Also list: scene entry variants of the next scene that apply under this branch (their `requires` are all true after the branch) and those that do not, and the branch's facts that the next scene never reads (no consumer with `scene_id` equal to the next scene or any later scene).
D. COMPARISON. After the per-branch sections, one comparison: for each fact set by some branches and not others, which later scenes read it; and the branches that leave no trace in any later scene.
E. EVIDENCE FOR JUDGMENT (Layer 4, never pass/fail). For each branch print, side by side and quoted, the branch's delivery text, the bridge text and the next scene's applicable entry text (base text plus applicable variants), headed by one sentence that says a reader decides whether the next scene follows from this branch; the tool does not decide.

FILES. /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/branch_report.py exposes `render_branch_report(root, incident_id)` and raises ValueError with a clear message for an unknown or non-incident anchor. /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/branch_report.py `scripts/branch_report.py <incident>` mirrors /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/impact_report.py (put the repo and worldkeeper src on sys.path the same way; exit 0 with the report, exit 2 with the message on ValueError). /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/docs/story-gap-guide.md: add a short section "Branch report" under Tool and status naming the command and what it shows, in the document's plain style, no story names.

HARD RULES. /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/branch_report.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/branch_report.py and /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/storygame/story_package/dependencies.py contain NO story names (no memory_card, kristin, patrol, laptop, k_sl_, t_1a, pursuit_1b, continuity, rebecca, brandon, michelle) even in comments or strings; the report works from whatever package it loads. Keep it story-agnostic: do not special-case any fact. No stored lists of accepted results.

TESTS in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_branch_report.py, pytest, hermetic. Build seeded defects by copying the real package directory into tmp_path and editing the copied YAML (follow the pattern of the seeded tests in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_gap_rules.py, which you may read). Required cases, each with a clean variant that gives no such result:
1. A branch declares a cost its realization never sets, and one it sets that nothing reads: assert the report states each.
2. A next-scene entry variant that requires an advantage one branch sets: assert it is shown as applying for that branch and not for the other.
3. The next scene's entry placements move an item the protagonist held at the end of the branch: assert a loss-of-custody move result naming the item and both places; the clean variant leaves the item where it was.
4. A branch after which no next-scene transition can fire: assert the dead-end result; the clean variant has no such result.
5. The real package: assert that for the incident with scene id 2C (find it by `scene_id == "2C"` in `package.incidents`), the report names the two declared costs that nothing reads, shows the entry variant that applies only after the rescue-style branch, and that rendering never raises. Print nothing for the whole story in this test; do not pin every line, pin only these facts. The real-package case may use story ids in the TEST file only.
6. `render_branch_report` raises ValueError for a pacing event id and for an unknown id.
Existing tests in /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_gap_rules.py, /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_impact_report.py and /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/tests/test_situation_trace.py must still pass.
